head.name: @fzlt/core/fx
head.lead: Explosions that land. One fixed pool of particles (struct-of-arrays, no allocation), drawn on a canvas: square debris, flashes, shock rings, spinning square rings, smoke, scorch marks and pop words, plus screen shake. blast() is the DOM VIRUS / Battlefield hero recipe. Gravity (gravity, px/s²) pulls each kind by its own share. Particle kinds are data (shape, drag, gravity, how they leave an emitter): emitter(fx, KINDS) registers the built-in bubble, spark, drip and debris (or your own) and sprays them; a page that never calls it never ships it. Visual only: its own random (seeded from Math.random), never the simulation's seeded random.

items.doc: Overload policy: particles are decorative, so a full pool refuses new ones and counts them in dropped; a blast stops its per-particle work as soon as the pool is full. Invalid input (non-finite numbers, a life that would never end) is refused and counted the same way.

items.doc: Named particle kinds on a pool: const { ids, emit } = emitter(fx, KINDS), then emit(ids.bubble, x, y, 12). Its own export, so a page that never sprays kinds never ships it. At most 26 kinds per pool (ids 6-31); a second emitter on the same pool adds after the first.
